<!-- ============ WHY MAP (SPLIT) ============ -->
<section class="lp-section lp-why">
  <div class="lp-container lp-split">
    <div class="lp-split-text">
      <span class="lp-eyebrow lp-eyebrow-pill">WHO Collaborating Centre</span>
      <h2 class="lp-h2">Learn the methods MAP uses to inform global malaria policy.</h2>
      <p>
        MAP is a designated World Health Organization Collaborating Centre in
        Geospatial Disease Modelling. Through this partnership, we provide
        modelling and analysis directly to the WHO Global Malaria Programme —
        with estimates cited in the World Malaria Report and the Global
        Burden of Disease study.
      </p>
      <p>
        This training is taught by the same scientists producing that work.
        You'll learn the exact methods MAP uses to inform global and national
        malaria policy.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="lp-split-visual">
      <div class="lp-medallion">
        <span class="lp-medallion-mark">WHO</span>
        <span class="lp-medallion-label">Collaborating Centre in<br>Geospatial Disease Modelling</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============ IMPACT (BIG MAP) ============ -->
<section class="lp-section lp-impact">
  <div class="lp-container">
    <div class="lp-section-header">
      <span class="lp-eyebrow">From Data to Decisions</span>
      <h2 class="lp-h2">Modelled malaria risk across Africa</h2>
      <p>
        Every cohort works with real spatial data, producing risk surfaces
        like the one below using the same Bayesian geostatistical methods
        taught in the programme.
      </p>
    </div>
    <figure class="lp-map">

    </figure>
  </div>
</section>
